purpose: Determine whether authored nonparallel locks, increased child density, explicit front-layer separation, staggered scalp roots or front-grid pruning can remove the procedural forehead bands.

r372.change: Replaced 22 evenly spaced micro-clumps with 14 manually parameterized locks controlling width, sweep, lift, length and end fan.
r372.finding: Lock direction is less uniform, but low final-fiber density exposes more individual strokes.

r373.change: Raised followers per guide from 18 to 42, raised front-lock fibers from 840 to 1,540 and reduced individual secondary radii.
r373.finding: The outer mass becomes more continuous, but several wide dark bands remain across the forehead.

r374.change: Separated scalp, primary, secondary, hairline and authored-front-lock geometry into five independently addressable layers.
r374.finding: Hiding the authored front locks does not remove the bands. Layer isolation proves the artifact originates in the primary/secondary scalp guide grid.

r375.change: Replaced 22 regular scalp rows with 46 staggered rows, deterministic two-axis jitter and fewer columns per row.
r375.finding: Root rows are less regular but still converge into a few visible front trajectories; the approach treats guides as final hair and preserves the underlying artifact.

r376.change: Removed all 185 primary/secondary guides classified as front while retaining the dedicated hairline and authored-lock layers.
r376.finding: The bands disappear only because the forehead coverage disappears. The density foundation and short locks are exposed as a cap and sparse fringe.

rootCause: The front-region scalp guides are arranged and curved as a small number of converging trajectory families, and their followers are rendered directly. Density and root jitter cannot hide the resulting bands; removing the families removes necessary coverage.

strictDecision.reason: No r372-r376 experiment exceeds the r371 overall visual result.

nextRequiredWork: Create a separate front-region surface-streamline field with continuous root distribution and controlled overlapping macro locks, then bake that high-density field to layered Aevrynd-owned hair cards for runtime. Preserve r371 skin/contrast and collision baselines.
